works.abstract: Verifying the presence of floating debris is vital for low-cost autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) involved in early marine pollution detection. Although traditional image-based analysis is a good starting point for verification tasks, there are specific difficulties associated with the process of operating under real-life water-surface conditions, which include seaweed, surface glare, far-away structures, and low-contrast images. This paper presents a deployment-based evaluation of the YOLOv8n-based RGB debris verifier specifically built for low-cost ASVs. We trained a YOLOv8n model on a publicly available bottle-oriented dataset. Our stress-test analysis is based on a specially reconstructed dataset of 145 images. On that data set, our detector showed average values of precision = 0.947, recall = 0.930, mAP@0.5 = 0.960, and mAP@0.5:0.95 = 0.831. Alongside these overall scores, we provide per-category statistics and confidence-threshold sweep data in order to show strengths and failures of the verifier. We observed 0.977 precision and 0.959 recall on the bottles-only subset; 0.610 and 0.667 false positives per image on the open-ocean and seaweed subsets, respectively; and no false positives on the limited 5-image glare subset. The confidence-threshold sweep allowed us to show how precision and recall can be tuned, which can be used for further deployment decisions regarding the trade-off between false-positive and missed-debris costs. Each per-category finding discussed below suggests a corresponding deployment or architectural mitigation.
works.title: Deployment-Based Hard-Negative Stress Test of Marine Debris Detection Using Water-Dependent Negative Examples for Resource-Constrained ASVs
